description:
Found by the fz-kdt.125 cold review (2026-09-01): lower_materialized_
call_target builds dispatch arms with marshals=None into callees whose
param_reprs the caller cannot satisfy, and NOTHING checks agreement.
The interp catches it late (direct_callable_capture_lanes errors on
the wrong fn id); native does not catch it at all -- it aborts inside
fz_unbox_int when a ValueRef closure word lands in a RawInt capture
lane (the fz-kdt.125 captures-variant abort). Cheap, high-value
red-first ASSERT at arm construction: an arm's callee param_reprs must
be satisfiable from the caller's lanes + declared marshals; violation
is a compile-time invariant failure, not a runtime tag abort. Lands
naturally with or after fz-kdt.125 (which removes today's known
violating arms by routing correctly).

comments.text:
PARTIALLY LANDED with fz-kdt.125 (2026-09-01), and the measurement changes what
is left.

THE VIOLATING ARM IS GONE, but not by an assert: `encode_runtime_value`'s
ShapeDescr::Callable branch used to push the caller's whole closure ValueRef as
though it were the callee's capture lane (jobs/native.rs, one line:
`lanes.push(*var)`). That is the fz-kdt.125 captures-variant abort in
fz_unbox_int. It now emits `Prim::ClosureCapture` per capture lane, reading each
slot back through the boundary that wrote it, so the encoder is total: every
shape it cannot bridge already returns `incomplete_native_program`, and the one
silent path is closed.

THE REMAINING HALF IS REAL AND STILL OPEN: a declarative "an arm's callee
param_reprs must be satisfiable from the caller's lanes" assert at arm
construction. It did not land because the fact it needs is not carried where the
arms are built. `lower_materialized_call_target` (jobs/artifact.rs) sees the
callee's `BackendSemanticInputLayout.reprs` and the caller's value LAYOUT, but
the caller's produced lane REPRS are decided later, in codegen; comparing
shapes instead would mean re-deriving the encoder's bridge relation beside it,
which is the duplication this ticket should not create. Two candidates worth
pricing when picked up: publish the caller's per-argument lane reprs as an
artifact fact so the comparison is a fact-to-fact one, or move the assert into
`native_direct_call_target_and_args` where both sides are in hand.

ONE NEW COMPILE-TIME INVARIANT DID LAND, in the same spirit:
`lower_closure_capture` refuses when a callable minted at several capture
layouts has boundaries that disagree about a slot's representation -- which is
fz-kdt.127's samelambda3 shape. Corpus fallout zero.

title: A dispatch arm must not name a callee whose ABI the caller cannot satisfy
